You see, all you need is faith to be saved according to Romans 10:9-10. You don't need to work your way into heaven like other religions teach you. You can rest in the finished work of Jesus Christ. But shall we continue to freely & willfully sin without care though we are saved? Certainly not! For in doing so we would be abusing the grace of God, & it wouldn't be right to continue to commit the very thing that made Christ have to die for us. This is called being lukewarm, meaning that you're being fake which can actually lead to judgement. I encourage you to read your Bible to grow & learn more about God & the truth. God bless

replies.text:
I hope therapy benefits you! 

I don't know what your specific ailments are or what your individualized treatment plan is, but please don't reject yourself. The healing process is one of arduous humiliation that'll typically leave one feeling lonely and conflicted, yet it also means improving introspection, strengthening resilience, and practicing discernment in relationships 

What you're describing sounds like conflict. Here you are, a therapist on your side, and yet things don't seem joyous; you're probably considering if any assistance was needed if life will only derail you. 

Here's the thing...healing is linear. Mine isn't. Yours isn't. No one's is. You'll have days where you'll feel like jumping sometimes, and they must be taken seriously. No more sulking in despair; utilize your consciousness, lead yourself into breakthroughs.  

I've a friend who I thought would abandon me because of my mental disorders and general personality flaws; she has a good social life, demanding responsibilities, and beautiful characteristics on her side, which is why I feel like she'll leave thinking she's too good for me (which she is  sometimes). But every day, she reassures me that I'm only human and that nobody's perfect, and sometimes listens to my vents if necessary. 

Life sucks, dude. I don't know who you have as a mitigation. Perhaps the only person you have is yourself right now, and that's okay. Befriend yourself through good and bad, just to live one more day. 

Sending hugs.
